mentions.name: Ember
mentions.description: Ember is a day planner app with dynamic rescheduling: moving a task or changing how long it takes shifts everything scheduled after it, and the plan flows around fixed events like meetings instead of becoming stale. The current build is web + Capacitor, with a native Kotlin app in development to replace it, and full duplex voice models being explored so tasks can be added or moved by conversing with an agent.
mentions.problem: Most planners treat your schedule as fixed, so when a meeting runs long or a task takes longer than expected, the plan is wrong and you have to fix it by hand or give up on it.
mentions.source_excerpt:
For the past two years I've been working on my day planner app Ember.

Most planners treat your schedule as fixed, so the moment a meeting runs long or a task takes twice as long, the plan is wrong and you either fix it by hand or give up on it. In Ember, if you move a task or change how long it takes, everything after it shifts later, and it flows around fixed things like meetings.
